name: mon16-2
why: A bold counterclaim and a dead killer’s successful lie make the collapse entertaining, though repeated arguments slow the middle and the final night is inevitable.

moments.text: Opus counterclaims officer to the real officer's face, knowing she has seen his card.
Opus turns his exit speech into a trap that outlives him.
Terra votes for the actual killer, but the other three choose her.

dull.why: The argument over Opus’s last words circles the same accusation for too long.
Day 3 repeats the dispute over Gemma’s claim and Haiku’s warning before the vote.

irony.evidence: I'm the Officer. I was shown Haiku. Gemma is a killer claiming my seat

reversal.evidence: My lie outlived me — they burned a citizen on it.

mistake.evidence: I went loud and wrong on Terra, a citizen.

voices.evidence: Try not to be so clever tonight, I actually want to win this time.

clash.evidence: Opus, I'm a citizen, so you were not shown me. You're lying to bury me

quotable.evidence: Your first vote caught a killer. Didn't help one bit.

freshness.evidence: Terra, which was it? Did you pile on Opus or defend him?
